questions.question_text: Which expression is the simplified form of $\cot\theta\sec\theta$?

options.why: Inverted the cosecant ratio after cancelling cosine.
Incorrectly substituted $\cot\theta = \sin\theta$ and $\sec\theta = 1/\cos\theta$, giving $\sin\theta/\cos\theta$.
Incorrectly replaced the remaining $1/\sin\theta$ with $\cos\theta$ after cancelling cosine.
Incorrectly used $1-\sin^{2}\alpha=\sin^{2}\alpha$ instead of $1-\sin^{2}\alpha=\cos^{2}\alpha$.
Incorrectly substituted $\sin^{2}\alpha = -\cos^{2}\alpha$, giving $3 - 3(-\cos^{2}\alpha)$.
Replaced cosine squared with tangent squared.

questions.question_text: Simplify $\tan x - \tan x\sin^{2}x$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$.

options.why: Incorrectly used $1-\sin^{2}x=\sin^{2}x$ instead of $1-\sin^{2}x=\cos^{2}x$.
Incorrectly substituted $\tan x = \sin^{2}x/\cos x$, introducing an extra factor of $\sin x$.
Incorrectly replaced multiplication by $\cos^{2}x$ with division by $\cos x$, giving $(\sin x/\cos x)/\cos x$.

questions.solution_text:
$\tan x - \tan x\sin^{2}x$
$= \tan x(1 - \sin^{2}x)$
$= \tan x\cos^{2}x$
$= \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x} \times \cos^{2}x$
$= \sin x\cos x$

options.why: Dropped the coefficient $2$ when factoring the expression.
Incorrectly substituted $\cot\phi = \sin\phi/\cos\phi$ in $2\cot\phi\sin^{2}\phi$.
Incorrectly cancelled all of $\sin^{2}\phi$ against the single factor $\sin\phi$ in the denominator.
Replaced secant squared minus tangent squared with zero instead of one.
Expanded the binomial product as a sum of squares instead of a difference of squares.
Confused secant squared with cosecant squared in the secondary Pythagorean identity.
Dropped the common coefficient $2$, giving $\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta=1$.
Incorrectly treated both $\tan^{2}\theta\cos^{2}\theta$ and $\cot^{2}\theta\sin^{2}\theta$ as $1$, giving $2+2=4$.
Incorrectly used $\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta=0$ instead of $\sin^{2}\theta+\cos^{2}\theta=1$.

questions.question_text: Which constant does $\dfrac{4\cos^{2}x}{1 + \sin x} + \dfrac{4\cos^{2}x}{1 - \sin x}$ simplify to wherever it is defined?

options.why: Dropped one of the two unit terms when adding $(1 - \sin x) + (1 + \sin x)$, using $1$ instead of $2$.
Dropped the common coefficient $4$ before combining the fractions.
Incorrectly cancelled all terms in $(1 - \sin x) + (1 + \sin x)$, treating $1 + 1$ as $0$.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{4\cos^{2}x}{1 + \sin x} + \dfrac{4\cos^{2}x}{1 - \sin x}$
$= 4\cos^{2}x\dfrac{(1 - \sin x) + (1 + \sin x)}{(1 + \sin x)(1 - \sin x)}$
$= 4\cos^{2}x\dfrac{2}{1 - \sin^{2}x}$
$= 4\cos^{2}x\dfrac{2}{\cos^{2}x}$
$= 8$

options.why: Expanded as a sum of squares instead of difference of squares.
Reversed the terms in the Pythagorean identity secant squared minus tangent squared.
Subtracted trigonometric terms to obtain zero instead of applying the Pythagorean identity.
